A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
relationship norms are a double-edged sword in word-of-mouth marketing.

the presence of financial incentives in word-of-mouth marketing may be detrimental to the perceived sincerity of referrals, but this can be mitigated when the financial motives are disclosed and the relationship norm of market pricing is activated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of relationship norms on consumer behavior is often underestimated in the marketing literature.
the effects of relationship norms on consumer behavior may be more pervasive than commonly thought.
marketers should be careful when using financial rewards to incentivize referrals, because these incentives can undermine the perceived sincerity of referring customers.
